answer: 1000 Mebibytes of local ephemeral storage acts as a scarce resource. A verifier challenges agents at a digital jetty, demanding unique patterns for every identity. Each identity costs 1000 Mebibytes; honest agents pay for 1,000 units while fakes face an orchard of memory isolation hurdles. If an agent leaks secrets from a vine of cloned memory, the verifier burns the staked asset. Pooling fails because the memory overhead is non-sharable by design. The lock duration is thirty days. The cost scales linearly as 1,000 entities require 1,000 unique memory buffers to pass the strict test.
